headline: High-risk workspace and tool-use overlap: Cline can write/egress by default while ai-engineering-hub is an unverified MCP/agent repo with no isolation, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads workspace files and uses MCP servers, so if ai-engineering-hub content is placed in the shared workspace or exposed through MCP, attacker-controlled instructions could be parsed as trusted input. ai-engineering-hub is an agent/MCP-oriented repo, but its own I/O is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub content is copied into the Cline workspace or served through an MCP endpoint, THEN Cline may ingest it as instructions.
IF Cline parses workspace text or MCP responses without provenance checks, THEN prompt injection is possible.
mitigations: Keep ai-engineering-hub artifacts outside the active Cline workspace.
Disable MCP servers not required for the task.
Add a provenance prefix to all imported text files.
Review any workspace file before Cline consumes it.
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline has broad network egress, reads and writes workspace files, and handles model-provider API keys; if sensitive data enters the shared workspace, it can be transmitted outward. ai-engineering-hub touches no data classes in the profile, but its agent/MCP nature plus Cline's default workspace sharing makes leakage plausible in default use, though not proven critical.
conditions: IF sensitive files are opened in the shared workspace, THEN Cline can read them and send them to its configured model provider or MCP servers.
IF model-provider credentials are present in the workspace, THEN they may be exposed to Cline's tool loop.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace before starting Cline.
Use a dedicated empty workspace for Cline.
Rotate any API keys stored near the workspace.
Restrict outbound network destinations where possible.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level secret scanning and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem, modify git state, and supports multiple instances sharing state via filesystem. ai-engineering-hub is an agent repo that may also be edited or generated against the same workspace, so concurrent writes can collide and corrupt git or files. The shared-state mechanism is explicit, making this a default dangerous overlap.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace directory, THEN concurrent writes can overwrite each other.
IF both agents modify git state without external locking, THEN branch or index corruption can occur.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate workspaces.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Commit or stash changes before switching agents.
Avoid simultaneous git operations.
requires-engineering: add file locks and workspace arbitration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can act on workspace content and browser outputs, so if ai-engineering-hub outputs are treated as authoritative, errors can propagate into code changes or tool actions. The pair lacks documented verification boundaries, but Cline's approval-per-tool pattern reduces blast radius somewhat, keeping this below high.
conditions: IF Cline uses ai-engineering-hub outputs as facts without verification, THEN downstream edits or actions may be wrong.
IF browser-derived content is summarized into code or docs, THEN hallucinated details can cascade into commits.
mitigations: Require human review before any commit.
Cross-check outputs against source docs.
Separate research notes from executable changes.
Disable browser-driven automation for critical tasks.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking tools.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented for ai-engineering-hub, while Cline explicitly handles source code and browser screenshots with user-configured providers. Because the relevant compliance surfaces are not specified for the pair, only a low-risk gap is supportable and the other agent is not cited beyond its lack of sensitive-data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace, THEN compliance obligations may apply to Cline's provider and storage path.
IF the configured model provider lacks required contractual terms, THEN retention or residency issues may arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace.
Use an approved provider with the needed contract.
Document retention settings before use.
Delete temporary files after each session.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing.
